lessons.title: Flats, Villas, Plots and Co-Living: The Residential Menu

children.text: Walk into any property expo in Pune with ₹1 crore and you will be offered four very different things under the same "residential" banner: a 2BHK in a Wakad gated community, a row house on the city's edge, a plot in an approved layout an hour out, and a 3BHK already leased to a co-living operator. The brochures all say "investment". But one is a rental product, one is a lifestyle asset, one is a pure bet on land and one is a stake in someone else's operating business. This lesson sorts the residential menu so you know which dish you are ordering.

body.text: A flat earns rent, a plot earns only land appreciation, a villa buys space and privacy, and co-living earns what an operator can squeeze from each bed. Same label, four different investments.

children.text: Apartments: The Default Choice

Apartments are the most traded residential asset in India for good reasons. They are standardised, easy for banks to value and lend against, and easy to rent. A 2BHK near a job hub is the most rentable configuration in most cities, because it suits young couples, small families and flat-sharing professionals alike.

Within apartments, the big split is between gated communities and standalone buildings. Gated projects with a clubhouse, security and power backup attract better tenants and resell faster, but charge higher monthly maintenance. Standalone buildings are cheaper to hold but rent and resell to a smaller pool.

body.text: For a rental investor, the best apartment is rarely the fanciest. A well-maintained 2BHK within a short commute of a large employer usually beats a 4BHK sky villa on yield, vacancy and resale time.

children.text: Know What You Are Paying For: Carpet vs Super Built-Up Area

markDefs.definition: The extra area added on top of carpet area to arrive at super built-up area, covering walls, balconies and your share of common areas. Expressed as a percentage of carpet area.

children.text: Before comparing any two flats, convert their prices to the same area measure. Developers historically quoted prices on super built-up area, which adds a share of lobbies, lift wells, staircases and the clubhouse to your flat. The gap between that and the space you can actually use is called
loading

cells: Net usable floor area inside the flat, including internal partition walls; excludes external walls, service shafts, exclusive balconies and open terraces
The legal basis for sale under RERA; the space you actually live in
Carpet area plus walls and exclusive balconies
Built-up area plus a proportionate share of lobbies, lifts, staircases and amenities
Common in older listings and resale quotes; inflates the area you appear to buy

body.caption: Always convert prices to rupees per sq ft of carpet area before comparing projects.

children.text: Example: a resale flat listed at 1,250 sq ft super built-up for ₹1 crore, which sounds like ₹8,000 per sq ft. Its carpet area is 875 sq ft. Loading is (1,250 minus 875) ÷ 875 × 100 = 42.9%, and the real price is ₹1 crore ÷ 875 = about ₹11,429 per sq ft of carpet. A neighbouring flat quoted at ₹10,500 per sq ft of carpet is actually cheaper.

body.label: RERA rule on area
body.value: Sale must be on carpet area
body.context: For RERA-registered projects, developers must state carpet area in agreements. Resale listings and older projects may still quote super built-up figures.

children.text: Builder Floors: Delhi NCR's Middle Path

markDefs.definition: An independent floor in a low-rise building constructed on a single plot, usually with three or four floors, sold separately. The buyer typically gets an undivided share of the land beneath.

children.text: A
builder floor

is one floor of a low-rise building on a single plot, common in South Delhi, Gurugram's DLF phases and Faridabad. You get more space and a share of the land at a lower price than a comparable independent house, with low maintenance. The trade-off is thinner amenities, variable construction quality, and approval questions that vary by state and locality. Resale buyers check those approvals closely, so paperwork gaps hurt liquidity.
Villas and Row Houses: Paying for Land and Privacy

Villas, independent houses and row houses carry a far larger land component than flats. That land is what tends to appreciate, while the building itself ages. The catch is rent: a villa costing twice as much as a flat rarely rents for twice as much, so yields are usually lower. You also bear more upkeep yourself, from waterproofing to garden maintenance. Villas suit investors who plan to live in the property eventually, or who are mainly betting on land value in a growing suburb.
Residential Plots: A Pure Land Bet

A plot earns no rent. What it offers is simplicity: no building to depreciate, no tenant to manage, low holding costs, and full appreciation of the land if the area develops. Buyers typically target plotted layouts on the growth edges of cities, such as along Hyderabad's Outer Ring Road or north Bengaluru near the airport.

markDefs.definition: Sanction from the planning authority, such as DTCP, HMDA or BMRDA, confirming the land is legally converted for residential use and the layout meets road, drainage and open-space norms.

children.text: The risks are concentrated in paperwork. A plot is only as good as its
layout approval

and title. Unapproved layouts can be denied building permission, bank loans or utility connections. Encroachment on vacant land is a real problem, and exits can take months because plot buyers are a narrower group. Bank finance for plots is also more restricted than for flats.

body.description: Every state has its own RERA portal. Search any project or plotted layout by name to see its registration, approvals and completion timeline before you pay a token amount.

children.text: Co-Living, PGs and Student Housing: Rent by the Bed

markDefs.definition: An agreement where an operator leases your whole property for a fixed rent over several years, then sub-lets rooms or beds to occupants and keeps the difference.

children.text: Co-living turns one home into several income streams by renting beds or rooms instead of the whole flat. Operators such as Stanza Living and Colive take entire flats or buildings near colleges and tech parks, furnish them and rent them per bed. As an owner, you either run a PG yourself or sign a
master lease
with an operator for a fixed monthly rent.

The appeal is a higher gross yield than a family rental. The cost is heavier wear and tear, dependence on the operator's own business staying healthy, possible objections from the housing society, and local licensing rules for PGs. If the operator exits, you inherit a furnished flat configured for sharing, which is not what a family tenant wants.

body.text: Short-stay rentals through platforms like Airbnb in Goa, Lonavala or Coorg look like residential property but behave like a hotel business: seasonal occupancy, cleaning and management costs, and tax treatment that can differ from ordinary rent. Model them as a business, not as a flat.

body.title: Quick Check: Match the Asset
body.question: Which residential option produces no rental income but also has no building that ages or depreciates?
options: A residential plot in an approved layout
A flat on master lease to a co-living operator
body.explanation: A plot is pure land. It earns nothing until sold or developed, but there is no structure to maintain or depreciate, so its return comes entirely from appreciation.

body.title: Calculate: Loading on a Pune Flat
body.prompt: A flat in Baner, Pune is advertised at 1,100 sq ft super built-up. Its RERA carpet area is 800 sq ft. What is the loading percentage?
body.explanation: (1,100 minus 800) ÷ 800 × 100 = 300 ÷ 800 × 100 = 37.5%. If the flat costs ₹88 lakh, that is ₹8,000 per sq ft of super built-up area but ₹11,000 per sq ft of carpet area.

body.title: Scenario: A Retiree Picks From the Menu
body.scenario: Lakshmi, 61, has retired in Coimbatore with ₹75 lakh to put into property. Her pension covers basic expenses, but she wants dependable monthly income to supplement it. A broker is pushing three options: a residential plot in a new layout near the upcoming bypass, a 2BHK flat in an established gated community near a large hospital, and a ground-floor independent house in an older neighbourhood that "will appreciate a lot".
body.prompt: Which option fits her goal best, and what would you tell her about the other two?
body.modelAnswer: The 2BHK near the hospital fits best. It can be rented from day one to doctors, nurses and staff who want a short commute, the gated community reduces maintenance headaches, and flats are easier to sell if she needs cash for medical costs later. The plot fails her main goal: it pays nothing, depends on the bypass actually being built, and could take months to sell. She must also verify the layout approval and guard against encroachment. The independent house may appreciate because of its land, but its rent will be low relative to the price, and she would carry all repairs herself. Neither of those two is wrong in general, they just answer a different question from the one she is asking.

body.title: Before You Buy a Residential Plot
steps: Confirm the layout approval from the planning authority (such as DTCP, HMDA or BMRDA) and match the plot number to the approved plan
Check RERA registration if the layout exceeds 500 sq m or 8 plots
Verify title and obtain an encumbrance certificate covering at least 30 years
Confirm the land has been converted for residential use
Visit the site in person and check road access, drainage and neighbouring encroachments
Ask two or three banks whether they will lend against plots in this layout
Plan how you will fence and monitor the plot while you hold it

cards.definition: Net usable floor area of a flat, including internal partition walls but excluding external walls, service shafts, exclusive balconies and open terraces.
Built-up area plus a proportionate share of common areas such as lobbies, lifts and amenities.
The percentage by which super built-up area exceeds carpet area.
An independent floor in a low-rise building on a single plot, common in Delhi NCR.
Planning authority sanction confirming a plotted development is legally converted and meets norms.
A fixed-rent lease of your entire property to an operator who sub-lets rooms or beds.

points: Residential property includes very different investments: flats earn rent, plots earn only appreciation, villas trade yield for land and space, and co-living depends on an operator.
A 2BHK near a major employer is usually the most rentable and liquid residential product.
Always compare flats on rupees per sq ft of carpet area; loading on super built-up quotes can exceed 40%.
Builder floors and villas carry a larger land share but lower yields and more paperwork or upkeep risk.
Plots are simple to hold but earn nothing, are slower to sell and are only as safe as their layout approval and title.
Co-living and short-stay rentals can lift income, but they behave like operating businesses with their own risks.

body.text: Prices, rents and yields in this lesson are illustrative and vary widely by city, micro-market and property. Approval authorities and rules differ by state. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy any property.
